title: Titles of shared notes from /api/shared are inserted as raw HTML
evidence: app.js:46 maps server records into an HTML string and passes it to insertAdjacentHTML. Nothing escapes s.title. The records are written by other users, so the sink crosses a trust boundary. Traced; the browser was not driven.
failing_case: Another user shares a note titled . Anyone who types a search that makes /api/shared return it runs that script on this origin. It can read every note in localStorage and send them out.
remediation: Build the nodes with createElement and textContent (or escape at one helper) and never concatenate server fields into HTML. Add a Content-Security-Policy without unsafe-inline as a second layer.

title: Note title is written into innerHTML unescaped (stored XSS)
evidence: app.js:10-12 builds the list row with a template literal and assigns it with list.innerHTML +=. n.title comes from the title input (store.js:16) and from localStorage. No escaping or textContent is used anywhere. Traced.
failing_case: Type in the title field, wait 500 ms, then click New note or search. renderList runs, the title is parsed as HTML and the onerror handler executes. It runs again on every page load because the title is persisted.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent (or escape &, <, >, quotes in one helper) and attach the delete handler with addEventListener.

title: Delete is immediate and permanent with no confirm or undo
evidence: removeNote calls deleteNote and persist at once (app.js:23-28, store.js:29-32). There is no confirmation, no undo and no trash. The 🗑 target is 20 px wide with opacity 0 until hover, next to the row that opens the note. Traced.
failing_case: The user aims for a row, clicks the right edge, and the note and its body are gone from localStorage with no way back.
remediation: Show an 'Undo' toast for about 8 seconds before the delete is persisted, or soft-delete into a trash list. A confirm dialog is the minimum.

title: Search responses are applied out of order and appended to whatever is on screen
evidence: Each keystroke fires a fetch with no debounce, abort or sequence check, then runs insertAdjacentHTML on the live list (app.js:40-47). Another interleaving: openNote or removeNote re-renders the list, and a late response is still appended. Traced.
failing_case: Type 'ab' quickly. The response for 'a' takes 800 ms and the response for 'ab' takes 100 ms. The list shows results for 'ab', then results for 'a' are appended under it. The user sees shared notes that do not match the box.
remediation: Debounce the input, give each request an AbortController (or a counter) and ignore any response that is not the latest. Render shared results from state, not by appending to the DOM.

title: The viewport meta blocks pinch zoom
evidence: index.html:5 sets maximum-scale=1. Combined with 12 px hint text and a fixed 1200 px layout, zoom is the only way a low-vision phone user can read the page. WCAG 1.4.4 (AA).
failing_case: On a phone, the user pinches to enlarge the note list. Mobile browsers that honour the attribute refuse.
remediation: Use `width=device-width, initial-scale=1` and drop maximum-scale and user-scalable.

title: Title and body fields have no label, and search uses its placeholder as the label
evidence: index.html:13 (#search has a placeholder only), 19 (#title) and 20 (#body) have no <label>, aria-label or placeholder. The title field is also empty-looking with a #eee border (1.16:1).
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' for the title and body fields. A sighted user sees two unlabelled boxes and cannot tell which is the title. When the user types, the search placeholder disappears. WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2 and 4.1.2 (A).
remediation: Add visible <label for> elements ('Title', 'Note', 'Search notes') or at least aria-label on each, and give the title a placeholder such as 'Untitled'.

title: Unguarded JSON.parse at load kills the whole app on bad or old saved data
evidence: store.js is the first script. A throw here leaves `notes` undefined, so app.js throws a ReferenceError at app.js:6 and nothing renders. Valid JSON of the wrong shape (an object, or records without `title`) passes the parse and then fails at `n.title.toLowerCase()` (app.js:6). There is no schema version. Traced.
failing_case: localStorage 'notes' holds '{bad' (an interrupted write or a manual edit). The page loads blank, with no message. The only way out is clearing site data, which destroys the notes. A record saved without a title crashes the list the same way.
remediation: Wrap the load in try/catch. Validate it as an array of {id, title, body, updated} and coerce missing fields. Keep the raw string under a backup key and tell the user what was recovered. Store a version number with the data.

title: Pending edits are dropped when the tab is closed or reloaded
evidence: The only write path is a 500 ms timer. There is no pagehide, visibilitychange or beforeunload listener anywhere in store.js or app.js (all four payload files read).
failing_case: Type a sentence into the body and reload or close the tab within 500 ms. The text never reaches localStorage, while the page says 'Changes save automatically'.
remediation: Add a flush() that performs the pending save synchronously and call it on pagehide, on visibilitychange to hidden, and before switching notes.

title: The debounced save writes to whichever note is current when the timer fires
evidence: scheduleSave captures nothing at schedule time. The timeout reads currentNote and the live field values after 500 ms (store.js:15-19). openNote replaces currentNote and the field values at once (app.js:16-21). Traced.
failing_case: Open note A and type 'edit of A' in the body. Within 500 ms click note B. The fields now show B, and the timer writes B's text into B. A's edit is never stored and nothing says so. A related case: click delete on the open note within 500 ms. currentNote becomes null and the timer throws a TypeError.
remediation: Capture the note id and the field values when scheduling. Flush or cancel the pending save inside openNote and removeNote before switching, and write only to the captured note.

title: Every save overwrites the whole stored array from this tab's memory (second tab destroys the first tab's notes)
evidence: notes is loaded once at script start (store.js:2). Each persist writes the entire in-memory array. No storage event listener, no merge, no version. Traced.
failing_case: Open the app in two tabs. Create note X in tab 1. In tab 2 (which has not seen X) edit any note; tab 2's persist writes its array without X and X is gone.
remediation: Listen to the storage event and reload or merge, or re-read before writing and merge by id and updated time.

title: Write failures (quota, private mode) are swallowed while the UI promises autosave
evidence: persist() ignores setItem errors and returns nothing (store.js:23-27). Callers cannot tell. index.html:21 states 'Changes save automatically'. Traced.
failing_case: localStorage is full, or blocked in a private window. setItem throws, the catch eats it, and the user writes for an hour. After a reload everything since the last successful write is gone.
remediation: Return a result from persist(). On failure show a persistent error ('Not saved: storage full. Export your notes or free space') and change the hint from 'Changes save automatically' to a state that reflects the outcome.

title: Fixed 1200 px layout scrolls sideways on phones and at 200% zoom
evidence: The container is a fixed 1200 px and the grid is `300px 1fr` with no media query anywhere in styles.css. At 390 px the page is about 3x wider than the viewport. At 200% zoom on a 1360 px desktop the 1200 px container is wider than the 680 px CSS viewport. The viewport is also locked against zoom. Traced from the CSS.
failing_case: Open the app at 390 px wide: the user has to pan horizontally to reach the editor, and the list and editor are never visible together. WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (AA).
remediation: Use `max-width: 1200px; width: 100%; padding: 0 16px` and a single column below about 720 px (grid-template-columns: 1fr), with the editor under the list or in a separate view.

title: Focus outline is removed from every control with no replacement
evidence: styles.css:6 is the only focus rule, and it has no :focus-visible substitute. Borders on the inputs are #eee (1.16:1 against white, measured), so the border is no focus cue either. Traced from the CSS.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabbing through search, New note, title and body cannot tell which control has focus. This is WCAG 2.4.7 (AA).
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3730a3; outline-offset: 2px; } that has at least 3:1 contrast against its neighbours.

title: Several text colours fail the 4.5:1 contrast minimum
evidence: Contrast I computed from the WCAG formula: #ccc on #fff is 1.61:1 (the autosave hint, styles.css:15). #bbb on #fff is 1.92:1 and #bbb on #eef (the active row) is 1.67:1 (styles.css:11, the rank badge). White on #8b5cf6, the right end of the hero gradient, is 4.23:1 for the 16 px intro line (styles.css:3). White on #6366f1 is 4.47:1 for the 13 px button label (styles.css:5).
failing_case: A low-vision user cannot read the hint that says whether the changes are saved, or the rank badge. WCAG 1.4.3 (AA).
remediation: Use at least #595959 for the hint and rank text. Use a darker indigo such as #4f46e5 for the button and the hero background (#4338ca at both ends clears 7:1 with white). Define the colours once as CSS variables.

title: Notes cannot be opened or deleted by keyboard or screen reader
evidence: Opening is a click handler on a plain <li> (app.js:30-33). Deleting is a click handler on a <div> holding an emoji. Neither has tabindex, a role, a key handler or an accessible name. Traced.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs from #search and #new to the title field. No list item is ever focused, so no existing note can be opened. The delete control cannot be reached. A screen reader announces the trash control as 'wastebasket' at best. This is WCAG 2.1.1 and 4.1.2, level A.
remediation: Make each row a <button> (or a link) that opens the note, and give delete its own <button aria-label="Delete note: TITLE"> outside the open button. Keep the visible focus style.

title: scheduleSave throws when no note is selected (first run, after delete)
evidence: currentNote starts null (store.js:3). The title and body inputs are always enabled (index.html:19-20) and wired to scheduleSave (app.js:36-37). The timer callback dereferences currentNote without a guard. After removeNote sets currentNote = null (app.js:26) the same happens. Traced.
failing_case: First run with no notes: type into the title field. 500 ms later the timer throws 'Cannot set properties of null (setting title)'. The typed text is not saved, and no message is shown.
remediation: Disable the editor until a note is open, or create a note on first input; guard the callback with if (!target) return.

quote: const sorted = notes.slice().sort((a, b) => b.updated - a.updated);
title: renderList copies and sorts every note once per visible note, and appends with innerHTML +=
evidence: The sort is inside shown.forEach (app.js:7-9), then indexOf is a linear scan. `list.innerHTML +=` re-serialises and re-parses the whole list for each item (app.js:10). Cost per render is about n sorts of n log n, plus n DOM re-parses. It runs on every search keystroke (app.js:42). Traced from the code; not timed.
failing_case: With 500 notes, each keystroke in the search box does 500 sorts of 500 items and 500 full re-parses of the list. Typing visibly lags, and 5,000 notes freezes the tab.
remediation: Sort once outside the loop and build a Map of id to rank. Build the markup in one string or a DocumentFragment and assign it once. Debounce the search.

title: Clicking a shared result throws and breaks the open note
evidence: Shared rows (app.js:46) are `li` elements with no data-id and the pointer cursor from `#list li` (styles.css:9). The delegated handler matches them. Number(undefined) is NaN, notes.find returns undefined, and app.js:17 assigns currentNote = undefined before app.js:18 throws. Traced.
failing_case: The user searches, sees a shared result and clicks it. A TypeError appears in the console and nothing opens. currentNote is now undefined while the editor still shows the old note, so the user's next edits throw in the save timer and are lost.
remediation: Ignore rows without data-id, or give shared rows their own action (open read-only, or copy into the user's notes). Make openNote return early when the id is not found.

title: Failed or non-JSON shared-search responses are only logged
evidence: res.ok is never checked, so a 404/500 HTML page reaches res.json() and throws. The catch writes to the console. The user sees no error, and a 200 with zero results looks the same as a failure. Traced.
failing_case: The server returns 500 or the user is offline. Search silently shows only local notes, as if no shared notes exist.
remediation: Check res.ok, and show an inline status ('Shared notes unavailable. Showing your notes only') with a retry. Show an explicit 'No shared notes' state for an empty result.

title: No empty state for a new user or for a search with no matches
evidence: The list is a bare <ul>. On first run, after deleting the last note, or when the filter matches nothing, it renders nothing (app.js:4-14). No copy tells the user what to do. Traced.
failing_case: A first-time visitor sees a banner, a search box, a button, a blank column and an editor they cannot save from (see the null currentNote finding). Searching 'zzz' shows a blank column that looks broken.
remediation: Render 'No notes yet. Choose New note to start.' when notes is empty and 'No notes match "zzz"' when the filter has no results. Disable the editor until a note is open.

title: The list never updates after an edit, so titles and ranks go stale
evidence: The save timer updates the data and persists (store.js:16-19) but never calls renderList. The list is rebuilt only on open, delete, new and search (app.js:20, 27, 42, 50). Traced.
failing_case: Create a note and type the title 'Groceries'. The list still reads 'Untitled' until the user clicks another row or searches. The '#rank' badge also stays at its old value after the edit makes the note the most recent.
remediation: Re-render (or update the single row) after each save, using the current search filter. Move DOM updates out of store.js.

title: The delete control is invisible unless the pointer hovers its row
evidence: styles.css:12 hides it with opacity 0 and reveals it only on :hover. There is no :focus-within rule, and the target is a non-focusable div. Touch screens have no hover.
failing_case: On a phone the user cannot see that notes can be deleted, but taps in the empty area on the row's right edge still delete the note (see the delete finding).
remediation: Keep the delete button visible at reduced emphasis, and reveal it on :hover and :focus-within. Give it a 44x44 px hit area.

quote: const note = { id: Date.now(), title: 'Untitled', body: '', updated: Date.now() };
title: Date.now() ids collide, and deleteNote removes every note with the same id
evidence: Id is the millisecond clock. deleteNote filters by id equality (store.js:30). Traced.
failing_case: Two New note activations in the same millisecond (double-click on fast hardware, a script, or a clock set back) create two notes with one id. openNote opens the first for both rows, and deleting either removes both, destroying a note the user did not delete. The same id also breaks the click delegation at app.js:32.
remediation: Use crypto.randomUUID() (store ids as strings and drop the Number() cast at app.js:32) and add a version field to the saved shape.

title: Deleting a note drops the active search filter
evidence: openNote passes the search value to renderList (app.js:20), but removeNote calls renderList() with no argument.
failing_case: Type 'milk' in search, delete one matching note: the list jumps back to every note while the search box still shows 'milk'.
remediation: Pass document.getElementById('search').value, or keep the filter in one variable that renderList reads.

quote: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, your notes, supercharged.
title: Placeholder text and a 'Welcome to' hero ship as user-facing copy
evidence: The hero reads 'Welcome to NoteMaster' with a ✨ emoji and 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet' in the first line users read. The hero takes about 190 px of height (60 px padding each side plus text) before the first control.
failing_case: Every visitor sees Latin filler under the heading. The banner also pushes the notes list below the fold on a 768 px high screen.
remediation: Replace the line with one specific sentence about what the app does, or drop the banner and make the search plus New note the first things on the page.
